# Baghdad 830 – Physics, optics & astronomy

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Ground lenses** [`lenses`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/lenses.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Burning glasses and burning mirrors are known from Greek books and the curiosity trade. Rock crystal is cut superbly in Basra and Iraq, glass is clearer than Rome's but still greenish. Nobody grinds a lens to see with. Local: rock-crystal cutters of Basra; glassmakers of Baghdad and Raqqa.
- **Spectacles** [`spectacles`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/spectacles.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept high. Old scholars and copyists lose their near sight and have pupils read aloud. A crystal cutter could grind convex lenses; the frame is the easy part. Ibn Masawayh's eye book has no remedy for it. Local: Yuhanna ibn Masawayh (Disorders of the Eye); copyists of the Suq al-Warraqin.
- **Law of refraction, image formation and vision** [`refraction_optics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/refraction_optics.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Euclid's Optics is being read in Arabic; rays leave the eye. Galen's eye anatomy puts sight in the crystalline humour. Ptolemy's refraction tables are not yet in Arabic. Al-Kindi will write on optics in Euclid's manner. Local: Ya'qub ibn Ishaq al-Kindi; Yuhanna ibn Masawayh.
- **Camera obscura** [`camera_obscura`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/camera_obscura.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. The crescent images of an eclipsed sun under leaves are a Greek curiosity. A dark room with a pinhole is an afternoon's work, and al-Ma'mun's astronomers would use it to watch eclipses safely.
- **Microscope** [`microscope`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/microscope.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. A fused bead of clear glass or a ground crystal sphere magnifies strongly; the glass here is good enough to try. Physicians would want proof that anything they saw mattered.
- **Telescope (refractor)** [`telescope`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/telescope.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept high. Needs a convex objective and a concave eyepiece of clear material; rock crystal can be ground but no one has made a concave lens. Astronomers at Shammasiyya and generals on the frontier would pay. Local: Sanad ibn Ali (instrument maker).
- **Reflecting telescope** [`reflecting_telescope`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/reflecting_telescope.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept medium. Polished steel and bronze mirrors exist, and Greek texts on burning mirrors treat the parabola. Figuring one accurately and adding an eyepiece is beyond any workshop.
- **Achromatic lens** [`achromatic_lens`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/achromatic_lens.md) — K0, use none, make impossible, accept low
- **Spectrum and the nature of colour** [`spectrum_colour`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/spectrum_colour.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept low. Aristotle's Meteorology, known through Syriac and early Arabic summaries: the rainbow is reflection in cloud, colours are mixtures of light and dark. A glass flask of water or a rock-crystal prism shows the spectrum.
- **Spectral analysis** [`spectroscopy`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/spectroscopy.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low
- **Waves - sound and light** [`wave_nature_light_sound`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/wave_nature_light_sound.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. String ratios are known to court musicians and in Greek harmonic texts; al-Kindi will write the first Arabic music theory. Sound as moving air is Aristotelian; light as a wave is unheard of. Local: Ishaq al-Mawsili (court musician, the 'ud); Ya'qub ibn Ishaq al-Kindi.
- **Finite speed of light** [`speed_of_light`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/speed_of_light.md) — K1, use none, make very-hard, accept low. Aristotle says light is instantaneous, and the visual ray reaches the stars at once. No measurement is possible without a telescope and a precise clock.
- **Photography** [`photography`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/photography.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low. Alchemists know vitriols and alum but no strong mineral acids to make silver salts; nobody has noticed silver darken in light.
- **Lever, pulley, inclined plane (statics)** [`lever_mechanics_statics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/lever_mechanics_statics.md) — K3, use correct, make easy, accept high. Steelyards (qarastun) and balances are in every market and the mint. Archimedes' proof is not yet in Arabic; a treatise on the steelyard comes later with Thabit ibn Qurra. Builders and siege engineers work by rule. Local: market inspectors (muhtasib) checking weights; siege engineers with manjaniq.
- **Buoyancy and hydrostatics** [`buoyancy_hydrostatics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/buoyancy_hydrostatics.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept medium. The crown story is told, but On Floating Bodies is not in Arabic and specific weights are not measured (al-Biruni and al-Khazini do it later). The mint and the money changers would gain at once. Local: the mint (dar al-darb); money changers (sarrafun) of Karkh.
- **Falling bodies and projectiles** [`falling_bodies`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/falling_bodies.md) — K1, use wrong, make easy, accept low. Aristotle's Physics is just entering Arabic: heavier bodies fall faster, nothing moves in a void. Mu'tazilite theologians debate motion as discrete leaps of atoms. Nobody drops two weights to see. Local: Abu al-Hudhayl al-Allaf (atoms and motion); al-Nazzam (the 'leap', tafra).
- **Laws of motion** [`laws_of_motion`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/laws_of_motion.md) — K1, use wrong, make medium, accept low. Motion needs a mover; the air pushes a thrown stone on. Philoponus' impetus critique exists in Greek and Syriac and will feed later Arabic ideas of mayl. Kalam theologians say God creates each moment.
- **Universal gravitation** [`universal_gravitation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/universal_gravitation.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low. Heavy things seek the centre of the world (Aristotle). Brahmagupta's remark that the Earth attracts bodies may sit in the Sindhind material, unremarked. Needs laws of motion and elliptical orbits first.
- **Strength of materials and scaling** [`strength_of_materials`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/strength_of_materials.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Brick vaults, domes and the great arches of the Sasanian tradition are sized by experience. Timber is scarce and imported; there are no rules beyond the master builder's. Local: Taq Kisra at Ctesiphon (Sasanian vault, a day downstream).
- **Sundial and water clock** [`sundial_water_clock`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sundial_water_clock.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Five daily prayers make time-keeping a religious need; sundials and the muezzin set the hours. Water clocks from the Greek and Sasanian tradition exist; Harun sent Charlemagne a striking water clock in 807. Local: muezzins of the great mosques. Elsewhere: Aachen: the water clock Harun al-Rashid's envoys gave Charlemagne (807).
- **Mechanical clock (escapement, spring drive)** [`mechanical_clock`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/mechanical_clock.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Gear trains exist in astrolabes and in Greek automaton books, but no escapement. Seasonal hours dominate civil life while astronomers already reckon in equal hours. Elsewhere: Tang China: Yi Xing's water-driven armillary with a stop-release linkage (725).
- **Pendulum clock** [`pendulum_clock`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/pendulum_clock.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept medium. Needs a working escapement first. A bare pendulum counting beats would help the astronomers timing eclipses, who now use water clocks and star altitudes.
- **Air pressure and the barometer** [`atmospheric_pressure`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/atmospheric_pressure.md) — K1, use wrong, make medium, accept low. Aristotelians deny a void; kalam atomists accept one, a rare opening. Mercury and blown glass tubes exist; a metre-long sealed tube is a glassblower's challenge, not an impossibility. Local: glassblowers of Baghdad; Abu al-Hudhayl al-Allaf (void between atoms).
- **Air pump and vacuum experiments** [`air_pump_vacuum`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/air_pump_vacuum.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low. Hero's and Philo's pneumatic tricks are known in Greek and will be built by the Banu Musa. A tight cylinder, valves and a clear vessel are the obstacles.
- **Thermometer and temperature scale** [`thermometer_temperature`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/thermometer_temperature.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept medium. Philo's and Hero's air expanding with heat is in the Greek pneumatics. Galenic physicians grade drugs in four degrees of hot and cold, a scale with nothing to measure.
- **Specific and latent heat** [`latent_specific_heat`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/latent_specific_heat.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low
- **Heat as motion, conservation of energy, limits of engines** [`heat_energy_conservation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/heat_energy_conservation.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low. Heat is a quality or a fiery element. Kalam atomism treats heat as an accident God creates in atoms; no thought of motion as heat.
- **Weather instruments and forecasting** [`weather_instruments`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/weather_instruments.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Weather lore comes from star risings (anwa'), Aristotle's Meteorology and sailors' monsoon knowledge. Rain is rare and the Tigris flood matters more. A rain gauge or wind vane is easy; a barometer is not. Local: anwa' star calendars of Arab tradition; Basra ship captains (monsoon timing).
- **Spherical Earth and its size** [`round_earth_size`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/round_earth_size.md) — K3, use correct, make easy, accept high. Ptolemy's spherical Earth is standard among scholars. Al-Ma'mun's surveyors measured one degree of meridian in the plain of Sinjar (c. 827), about 56 2/3 Arabic miles; the length of the mile, and so the result, is still argued. Local: Khalid ibn Abd al-Malik al-Marwarrudhi; Ali ibn Isa al-Asturlabi; Sanad ibn Ali.
- **Cause of the seasons (tilted axis)** [`seasons_axial_tilt`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/seasons_axial_tilt.md) — K3, use correct, make easy, accept medium. The Sun's yearly circle is tilted about 23 1/2 degrees; Shammasiyya observers measure the obliquity afresh as about 23°33', smaller than Ptolemy's 23°51'. A tilted Earth moving around the Sun is the new part. Local: Yahya ibn Abi Mansur (Mumtahan observations).
- **Cause and prediction of eclipses** [`eclipse_prediction`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/eclipse_prediction.md) — K3, use correct, make medium, accept high. Court astronomers compute eclipses from the Almagest and Indian tables, and the caliph's men record observed ones to test the tables. For the street an eclipse calls for prayer, not fear of omen alone. Local: Habash al-Hasib; Yahya ibn Abi Mansur; Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi (zij al-Sindhind).
- **Heliocentric model** [`heliocentrism`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/heliocentrism.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept low. The Almagest, just in Arabic, refutes the moving Earth. Aryabhata's rotating Earth is faintly known from Indian material. No stellar parallax can be shown, and theologians would add scripture.
- **Kepler's laws of planetary motion** [`keplers_laws`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/keplers_laws.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low. Apollonius' Conics is known by name; the Banu Musa will have it translated. Tables are now good enough to show Ptolemy's errors, not to demand ellipses.
- **Distances of Moon, Sun and stars (parallax)** [`astronomical_distances`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/astronomical_distances.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept medium. Ptolemy's distances (Moon about 60 Earth radii, Sun about 1,200) are being taken over; al-Farghani will popularise them. Stars sit on one sphere just beyond Saturn. Local: Ahmad al-Farghani (young astronomer).
- **Comets as orbiting bodies** [`comets_orbits`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/comets_orbits.md) — K1, use wrong, make very-hard, accept low. Aristotle's comets are fires in the upper air; astrologers read them as signs of rulers' deaths. Chinese court records of comets go back a millennium. Elsewhere: Tang China: systematic comet records.
- **Tides caused by Moon and Sun** [`tides`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/tides.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Basra lives by the tide in the Shatt al-Arab, twice daily, and sailors tie it to the Moon. Abu Ma'shar will write the Moon theory of tides later; for now it is practical knowledge. Local: Basra boatmen and the tidal canals.
- **The Earth as a magnet** [`terrestrial_magnetism`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/terrestrial_magnetism.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Lodestone draws iron (Greek and Persian lore); that it points north is unknown here and not yet used in China either. Needs the compass first.
- **Deep time - age of the Earth, strata and fossils** [`deep_time_geology`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/deep_time_geology.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept low. Inland shells are a Greek remark; Aristotle's world is eternal. The eternity of the world versus creation in time is a hot kalam question, so geology quickly becomes theology.
- **Continental drift and plate tectonics** [`plate_tectonics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/plate_tectonics.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low
- **Stars as suns, galaxies and the expanding universe** [`stars_galaxies_cosmology`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/stars_galaxies_cosmology.md) — K1, use none, make very-hard, accept low. One finite cosmos of nested spheres (Ptolemy, Aristotle). The Milky Way as many faint stars is a Greek opinion found in commentaries. Kalam allows God to create anything, but not a universe of suns.
